$comment: Commands shipped code probes that are deliberately NOT declared as feature
dependencies, and why. Nothing reads this at runtime; it is the allow-list
scripts/check-command-declarations.py compares the probe sites against, so an
audit can tell a deliberate exclusion from drift. Adding a probe for a new
command means declaring it under "features" or adding it here — the check
fails otherwise, and it fails on a stale entry here that nothing probes.
`sudo` is absent on purpose: VGS-11 declares it under a sudo-toggle group.
undeclared.vshell: Self-reference: resolves the CLI's own path.
undeclared.quickshell: Alternative binary name for the already-declared `qs`.
undeclared.start-hyprland: Optional session wrapper in the greeter launch path; falls back to `Hyprland` directly.
undeclared.dbus-run-session: Wraps the file manager when generating committed theme previews. Repo tooling, not a runtime feature.
undeclared.nvim: Theme-reload hook for an editor you may not use. Declaring it would make `deps status` report a missing dependency for everyone who does not run nvim.
undeclared.gdbus: Fallback path of the ghostty theme-reload hook, behind a SIGUSR2 attempt. Same reasoning as `nvim`.
undeclared.magick: Third choice in the wallpaper-thumbnail chain, behind Pillow and the already-declared `ffmpeg`.
undeclared.xclip: X11 clipboard fallback behind the declared `wl-copy`. Unreachable in a supported Hyprland/Niri session.
undeclared.xdg-terminal-exec: First choice of the terminal resolver, but it *launches* a terminal rather than being one: counting it as an alternative in the `terminal` group would report that group available on a system with no terminal at all, which is the VGS-54 defect. AUR-only, so it can never be a requirement either.
undeclared.g++: Compiles the vendored third_party/asdcontrol for Apple display brightness. The preferred Apple path is pure-Python hidraw and packaging can ship a prebuilt binary, so a compiler is not a dependency of the feature.
undeclared.c++: Alternative compiler name, same reasoning as `g++`.
undeclared.uwsm: Deferred to VGS-32, which centralises how VGS launches external apps. Hardcoded today in the vgsMenu catalog and the screensaver launcher; declaring it now would entrench the choice VGS-32 replaces.
undeclared.dconf: Alternative GTK settings backend, probed behind the already-declared `gsettings` (theme-gtk).
undeclared.dcal: Second calendar backend, probed behind the declared `khal`. No distribution packages it, so declaring it would make `deps status` ask for something a user cannot install.
undeclared.tte: terminaltexteffects, the text-effect screensaver renderer. Distributed on PyPI rather than by the distributions VGS packages for, so it has no package name to report; the screensaver falls back to its other modes.
undeclared.zellij: Second multiplexer backend of the `mux` service, alongside the already-excluded `tmux`. Declaring it would tell every user to install a multiplexer.
undeclared.go: Builds the Go backend from source when no prebuilt binary is present. A packaging and development path with an already-built-binary fallback, not a runtime feature.
undeclared.nvidia-offload: Distro-provided dGPU offload wrapper, probed opportunistically when launching an app. Absent by design on a machine without an NVIDIA GPU.
undeclared.prime-run: Same as `nvidia-offload`; the other common wrapper name.
undeclared.secret-tool: Optional round-trip verification inside the keyring bootstrap, already behind its own `command -v` guard. The keyring itself is `gnome-keyring-daemon`, declared under `greeter`.
undeclared.mmsg: miracle-wm IPC, reached by the bar's Overview pill. VGS targets Hyprland or Niri only, so this probe can never succeed on a supported session: an unsupported-compositor leftover to remove, not a dependency to declare.
undeclared.yazi-scratchpad-open: Not shipped by VGS: a personal-overlay script reached by the capture helpers, behind a fallback. Recorded so the audit keeps seeing it; the same overlay-and-dependencies.md rule applies.

$comment: This manifest declares PRESENCE, not versions, and deliberately has no
version-constraint syntax — see docs/decisions/D005-dependency-version-constraints.md.
Where VGS needs more than presence, the check is a capability probe in
bin/vshell-helper's CAPABILITY_PROBES: it asks the installed command to do
the thing VGS depends on, and `vshell deps status` reports the failure as
"installed but unusable". That is the real check; this note is context.
jq: needs regex builtins (`test`, `match`, `sub`, `gsub`, including
three-argument `gsub($re; s; flags)`), which arrived together in jq 1.5
(2015-08-16) — jq 1.4 has none of them. Probed, not version-compared.
Launcher TEXT search. Missing means text search fails outright --
there is no fallback.
Launcher FILE and FOLDER search. Despite the name, fd is not an
optional accelerator: bin/vshell-helper keeps an os.walk fallback,
but the overview declines it and shows an install hint instead -- a
full walk of the search roots per query, with nothing cached between
them, cannot answer at typing speed. Missing fd/fdfind therefore
means no overview file or folder search, except folder completion
for a path query -- ~-rooted, or /-rooted through the '/d ' typed-type
prefix -- which the helper answers without fd. (A BARE leading / is
the launcher's own file-search trigger and is consumed before the
query reaches the helper; '/d ' consumes only itself.) Text search is
gated separately on rg and keeps working without fd. The vgsMenu
plugin is not gated and still reaches the walk.
mise installs coding-agent harnesses and language toolchains under
~/.local/share/mise; `vshell mise`, `vshell agent`, `vshell dev-env` and
the tools row of the System Updates widget all sit behind it.
The Sunshine host behind the remoteDesktop widget. The widget gates on
`vshell remote-desktop status`, which reads the systemd unit rather
than the binary, so it is correct even where the unit is installed
under a name this probe cannot see; the group exists so `deps status`
names the package a user has to install to get the widget at all.
hyprctl is declared under `hyprland` already: the virtual output half
is Hyprland-only and the host still runs without it.
Status and REVOKE, which deliberately need no terminal. The widget
gates on `vshell sudo-toggle status` rather than on deps, so the
safety valve works regardless; this group exists so `deps status`
says the same thing the runtime does. VGS-11 exists because gating
both directions on a terminal stranded machines in the escalated
state, so requiring `terminal` here would make the reporting layer
contradict a stated invariant.
The GRANT half only. Enabling passwordless sudo always goes through a
terminal so the user sees what is happening and sudo can authenticate,
so this half really is unavailable without one -- and saying so here is
what keeps the `sudo-toggle` group above honest about revoke.
